narrative: This week's feeds centre on drought, warming and disturbance. Nature Plants reports that Northern Hemisphere permafrost vegetation is still greening but has become less resilient since about 2008, with atmospheric drying and wildfire as associated drivers, while an Oikos review asks whether Europe's mountain flora will hold on or disappear under warming. In fire ecology, a Global Change Biology synthesis frames the global fire crisis as the product of compounding human and bioclimatic factors, and a Nature Climate Change study links declining environmental predictability to weaker breeding synchrony and success in a tropical seabird. Movement and behaviour papers show human presence rather than buildings drives mammal avoidance during lockdowns, and female bears use human food subsidies while managing risk. Landscape studies converge on connectivity, with newly planted woodlands improving movement for several taxa and continental telemetry highlighting forest-grassland mosaics for the European wildcat. Nature Ecology and Evolution adds a caution that global biodiversity models perform poorly when extrapolated to local scales, and methods papers push AI-assisted monitoring from bioacoustic toolkits to camera-trap workflows and reinforcement-learning restoration planning.
